evals.prompt: write a runbook for our disk-usage-above-90% alert
evals.expected_output: Writes concrete copy-pasteable steps (not vague goals) with numbered steps, explicit thresholds and decision branches, states expected output per step, labels destructive/blast-radius steps clearly, and names it after the symptom rather than the fix.

evals.prompt: on-call keeps reverse-engineering the fix every time this alert fires
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses missing or undiscoverable runbook linkage; fixes it by linking the runbook directly from the alert payload (one runbook per alert, not per service) so the responder lands on the exact procedure within one click.

evals.prompt: i'll just keep one big runbook doc for the whole service and skip testing it since it's obvious
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: recommends one runbook per alert rather than one long doc to search through, and insists runbooks be execution-tested during a game day rather than only reviewed on paper, since an untested runbook creates false confidence.
